examples.knowledge_point: Calculating the Distance Between a Particle and the Origin
examples.problem: A particle moves from the origin with an acceleration of $(\mathbf{i} +\mathbf{j}) \, \textrm{cm/s}^2$ and an initial velocity of $(-\mathbf{i}-2\mathbf{j}) \: \textrm{cm/s}.$ Find the distance from the particle to the origin after $6$ seconds.
examples.worked_solution:
If a particle moves with constant acceleration $\mathbf{a},$ the position vector of the particle at time $t$ can be found using

$$
\mathbf{r} = \mathbf{r}_0 + \mathbf{u} t + \dfrac12 \mathbf{a} t^2,
$$

 

where $\mathbf{r}_0$ is the initial position of the particle and $\mathbf{u}$ is its initial velocity.

In our case, we have

$$
\mathbf{r}_0 = 0\mathbf i +0 \mathbf j , \qquad \mathbf u = -\mathbf{i}-2\mathbf{j}, \qquad \mathbf a = \mathbf{i} +\mathbf{j}.
$$

Therefore, the position vector of the particle after $t = 6 \, \textrm{s}$ is

$$
\begin{aligned}r & =(0i+0j)+(-i-2j)(6)+\frac{1}{2}(i+j)(6)^{2} \\  & =(-6i-12j)+18(i+j) \\  & =(-6i-12j)+(18i+18j) \\  & =(12i+6j)\,\text{cm}.\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, the distance from the particle to the origin at this time is

$$
\begin{aligned}|r| & =|12i+6j| \\  & =\sqrt{{12}^{2}+{6}^{2}} \\  & =\sqrt{144+36} \\  & =\sqrt{180} \\  & =6\sqrt{5}\,\text{cm}.\end{aligned}
$$

feedback.problem: A particle starts moving from the point with position vector $(-i+j)\,\text{mm}$ with an acceleration of $(2i-6j)\,{\text{mm/min}}^{2}$ and an initial velocity of $(-3i+2j)\,\text{mm/min}.$ Find the position vector of the particle after $5$ minutes.
feedback.worked_solution:
If a particle moves with constant acceleration $a,$ the position vector of the particle at time $t$ can be found using

$$
r={r}_{0}+ut+\frac{1}{2}a{t}^{2},
$$

 

where ${r}_{0}$ is the initial position of the particle and $u$ is its initial velocity.

In our case, we have

$$
{r}_{0}=-i+j,\,u=-3i+2j,\,a=2i-6j.
$$

Therefore, the position vector of the particle after $t=5\,\text{min}$ is

$$
\begin{aligned}r & =(-i+j)+(-3i+2j)(5)+\frac{1}{2}(2i-6j)(5)^{2} \\  & =(-i+j)+(-15i+10j)+25(i-3j) \\  & =(-16i+11j)+(25i-75j) \\  & =(9i-64j)\,\text{mm}.\end{aligned}
$$
